newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Sept palm oil output up 3.4 pct - Ivan Wong.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Sept palm oil output up 3.4 pct - Ivan Wong.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in September is estimated to have risen by 3.4 percent to 838,000 tonnes over August, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Monday.
Wong had earlier forecast a four percent increase.
Palm oil stocks at end-September are estimated at 900,000 tonnes, down slightly from his earlier projection of 905,000 tonnes.
The official Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) put stocks at end-August at 800,893 tonnes.
Wong did not include export figures in his latest report. He had earlier estimated exports in September at 645,000 tonnes, against 638,601 tonnes in August.
Wong said output of major producers in Peninsular Malaysia ranged from up 10 percent to down eight percent while in East Malaysia, production ranged from unchanged to up 20 percent.

"Crude palm oil output of some mills were practically unchanged because the plant has reached full operating capacity," he said. "Some adjustments were made in terms of delaying the harvesting rounds. Consequently, crude palm oil production in East Malaysia should increase further in October."

Wong said crude palm oil stocks at the end of September are estimated to have risen to 550,000 tonnes from 472,200 tonnes a month earlier, while processed palm oil stocks increased to 350,000 tonnes from 328,693 tonnes at end-August.
Wong said several vessels scheduled to lift cargoes in September had apparently slipped into October.
